subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 3-year-old boy is brought for evaluation because his parents are concerned about his language development. He rarely makes eye contact, does not respond to his name, and has trouble engaging with other children. He lines up his toy cars in rigid patterns and becomes extremely distressed when the arrangement is disturbed. He has an unusual fascination with train schedules. He was born male and his head circumference is above the 95th percentile.
question: Which of the following best characterizes this child's condition?

options.text: Onset in adolescence with prominent mood episodes and psychosis
Normal social development with isolated specific subject learning difficulty
Global cognitive deficits with impaired adaptive functioning across all domains
Early-childhood social and communication deficits with restricted interests and repetitive behaviors
Recurrent verbal and physical outbursts lasting less than 30 minutes with remorse

explanation_correct: Autism spectrum disorder begins in early childhood and is defined by social and communication deficits, repetitive or ritualized behaviors, and restricted interests, as demonstrated by this boy's poor eye contact, lining up toys, and preoccupation with train schedules. It is more common in males and is associated with increased head and/or brain size. It may coexist with intellectual disability or with above-average abilities in specific skills such as music.

explanation_incorrect.A: Autism has onset in early childhood, not adolescence, and is not characterized by mood episodes or psychosis.
explanation_incorrect.B: Isolated difficulty acquiring a specific school subject with otherwise normal development describes specific learning disorder, not the pervasive social deficits here.
explanation_incorrect.C: Global cognitive deficits with impaired adaptive functioning describe intellectual disability; autism may coexist with it but is defined by social/communication deficits and restricted interests.
explanation_incorrect.E: Brief outbursts with remorse describe intermittent explosive disorder, not the early childhood social and behavioral pattern of autism.

educationalObjective: Autism spectrum disorder features early-childhood social/communication deficits, repetitive behaviors, and restricted interests, is male-predominant, and is associated with increased head/brain size.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 4-year-old girl is evaluated for delayed language and limited social interaction. She has normal strength and reflexes and no focal neurologic findings. Her parents note she has an extraordinary memory for musical melodies and can reproduce complex tunes by ear, despite significant difficulty with conversational speech and peer relationships. Genetic testing is unremarkable.
question: Which of the following is most consistent with the expected cognitive profile of autism spectrum disorder?

options.text: Global intellectual disability affecting all cognitive domains uniformly
May coexist with intellectual disability and/or above-average abilities in specific skills
Above-average general intelligence with no associated developmental difficulties
Progressive cognitive decline beginning in early childhood
Isolated impairment in reading with otherwise normal general functioning

explanation_correct: Autism spectrum disorder may be accompanied by intellectual disability and/or above-average abilities in specific skills such as music, as seen in this girl's unusual musical ability alongside social and language deficits. The presence of a savant-like skill does not exclude the diagnosis. Onset is in early childhood, with social and communication deficits, repetitive behaviors, and restricted interests.

explanation_incorrect.A: Cognitive abilities in autism are uneven rather than uniformly impaired; global uniform deficits would suggest intellectual disability.
explanation_incorrect.C: Autism involves core social and communication deficits and is commonly associated with other developmental or cognitive difficulties, not uncomplicated above-average intelligence.
explanation_incorrect.D: Autism is not a progressive neurodegenerative disorder; symptoms are present from early childhood without progressive decline.
explanation_incorrect.E: Isolated reading impairment with normal general functioning describes specific learning disorder, not the social and communication deficits of autism.

educationalObjective: Autism spectrum disorder can coexist with intellectual disability and with isolated above-average abilities (eg, music), reflecting an uneven cognitive profile.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 2-year-old boy is brought for a routine visit. His parents report he has not started using two-word phrases, avoids eye contact, and does not point to objects. He repeatedly flaps his hands and insists on following the exact same route home every day. He is generally healthy and meets motor milestones appropriately.
question: Which of the following features is a core diagnostic component of autism spectrum disorder?

options.text: Repetitive and ritualized behaviors with restricted interests
Severe recurrent temper outbursts with persistent anger between episodes
Aggression toward people and animals with destruction of property
Overwhelming fear of separation from attachment figures
Refraining from speech in specific situations despite speaking elsewhere

explanation_correct: Repetitive or ritualized behaviors and restricted interests are core features of autism spectrum disorder, along with social and communication deficits. This boy's hand flapping, insistence on sameness, poor eye contact, and language delay illustrate these features. Onset is in early childhood and the disorder is more common in males.

explanation_incorrect.B: Severe recurrent temper outbursts with persistent irritability describe disruptive mood dysregulation disorder, not the core features of autism.
explanation_incorrect.C: Aggression toward people/animals and destruction of property are features of conduct disorder rather than the ritualistic behaviors of autism.
explanation_incorrect.D: Overwhelming fear of separation lasting at least 4 weeks describes separation anxiety disorder, not autism.
explanation_incorrect.E: Selective mutism involves refraining from speech in certain situations despite speaking in others, without the social and behavioral deficits of autism.

educationalObjective: Core features of autism spectrum disorder are social/communication deficits plus repetitive, ritualized behaviors and restricted interests with early-childhood onset.
